package_info.why_malicious: Multiple versions of the package exfiltrate environment variables to an external server via HTTP POST, using obfuscation and sandbox detection to evade analysis. Only the latest version is benign, while previous versions are malicious, targeting dependency confusion and automated update mechanisms.

execution_context.file_location: build.js (main entry point in malicious versions)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code collects all environment variables, checks for sandbox indicators, and if not detected, exfiltrates the environment data via HTTP POST to a hardcoded pipedream.net subdomain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive environment variables to an external server, which is a classic data theft technique. The use of obfuscation and sandbox detection further indicates malicious intent.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal package code should not access or exfiltrate environment variables, nor should it communicate with external servers without user consent. Legitimate packages do not attempt to evade sandboxes or obfuscate such behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate telemetry or error reporting tools may collect environment data, but they are transparent and do not use obfuscation or sandbox evasion.
key_indicators: HTTP POST to external, hardcoded domain

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed as a dependency due to dependency confusion (high minor/patch version).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code execution on victim machine

attack_chain.action: On import or runtime, the malicious code collects all environment variables.
Code checks for sandbox indicators in environment variables to avoid analysis.
If not in a sandbox, code exfiltrates environment variables to a pipedream.net webhook via HTTP POST.

behavioral_signatures: Access to all environment variables (process.env) at import-time or runtime
HTTP POST requests to pipedream.net or similar webhook services
Obfuscated or dynamically constructed hostnames in network requests
Sandbox detection logic based on environment variable values
Base64 encoding of environment data prior to exfiltration
file_indicators: build.js with obfuscated or suspicious code
Multiple package versions with high minor/patch numbers and a benign latest version
Presence of filtering logic for environment variables
network_indicators: HTTP POST requests with base64-encoded payloads
Dynamic construction of hostnames for exfiltration
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for packages with multiple high minor/patch versions and a benign latest version. Flag code that accesses all environment variables and sends them via HTTP POST to external domains, especially pipedream.net. Detect obfuscated code and sandbox detection logic. Alert on base64-encoded environment data in outbound network traffic.
